messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty -> Severity 2: elevated DNS resolution failures observed from Azure eastus2 vWAN (affecting Private/VPN & ExpressRoute-connected workloads). Trigger: dns-failure-rate > 12% for 3m. Incident ID INC-202303. Paging @oncall-azure and infra team. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-202303
Amanda C.: oncall-azure acknowledged, tagging infra. I'm looking at Redwood edge metrics and customer error spikes.
Jonah R.: noticed a jump in `model-registry` lookups timing out from eastus2 starting ~2236999800. RTT for DNS queries -> 1000-3000ms and NXDOMAINs for some internal domains.
Mike L.: Confirmed. Our private DNS proxies (in eastus2 vnet) show increased `SERVFAIL` rates for queries to customer-managed DNS forwarders. Logs: `dnsproxy: upstream tcp timeout; retrying over UDP` repeated.
Sara P.: CS: getting inbound messages from 3 enterprise customers on Dedicated who report 5-10% inference failures and variable latencies. They're seeing failures from services pinned to eastus2.
Network Eng: from the network plane, Azure vWAN telemetry shows intermittent eBGP path flaps between our peering and customer ExpressRoute in eastus2 at the same time window. We're also seeing packet loss on some links -> could explain TCP timeouts to DNS forwarders.
oncall-azure: I'm taking lead. Immediate plan: 1) failover DNS queries in region to our secondary internal resolvers (eastus3) via route policy, 2) place temporary routing policy to prefer alternate path for customer ExpressRoute prefixes, 3) roll canary reroute for a small subset of tenants. Executing now.
Amanda C.: please post commands you run so we can audit and rollback if needed.
oncall-azure: running `az network vwan connection update --name <conn> --set routingPreference=PreferAlternate` on affected connections (canary set first). Also pushed a config to dns-proxy autoscale to spin up 2 extra instances in eastus3.
Mike L.: logs show our health-checks failing between eastus2 dns-proxy and customer forwarder on TCP/53. Running a remote tcpdump on proxy01-eus2: ```
09:45:12.123 IP proxy01-eus2.12345 > forwarder.tcp53: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0
09:45:12.223 IP forwarder.tcp53 > proxy01-eus2.12345: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0
...
```
Jonah R.: can confirm: after adjusting route to eastus3, our telemetry shows DNS latency drop to ~30-60ms for the canary traffic. No application errors for the canary.
CS Ops: Please prepare a short customer note: impacted customers are those with private deployments pinned to eastus2 vWAN/ExpressRoute and using customer-managed DNS forwarders. Estimated impacted: 12 Dedicated clusters and 7 Private VPC customers.
Sara P.: drafting now. ETA 10m. Will include mitigation steps and ask customers to report any residual issues.
Network Eng: continuing to monitor BGP session states. We're seeing spontaneous withdraws from one provider fabric in eastus2 — opening ticket with provider now. Reference: `AZ-VWAN-INC-789`
oncall-azure: I've expanded the alternate-route policy to all affected ExpressRoute circuits. Also enabled conditional fallback in our routing plane: prefer eastus3 route for DNS prefixes if latency > 250ms.
Amanda C.: good. Next: trigger cross-region failover for critical private endpoints if instability persists > 15m. Also schedule a canary rollback plan.
incident-bot: Update: mitigation actions applied at 2237000120. Automated check: canary = 1000 queries/5m -> success (error rate < 0.5%).
Mike L.: one remaining issue: some customer on-prem firewalls block traffic to eastus3 resolvers (they only allow eastus2 IPs). Need Customer Success to coordinate allowlist changes or we can NAT through eastus2 egress with our own resolver as a proxy.
CS Ops: noted. Reaching out to affected customers with instructions and optional temporary NAT proxy.
Jonah R.: adding runbook note to incident: `If eastus2 DNS flap persists, enable resolver-proxy in eastus2 to forward to eastus3 and NAT reply traffic through our egress IPs.` Snippet: ```
# enable proxy
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/services/dns-proxy/scale -d '{"region":"eastus2","target_instances":2}'
```
Amanda C.: that's the one. Also capture post-incident: root cause likely provider edge BGP instability causing packet loss to customer forwarders -> cascading DNS failures for private deployments. Need provider RCA.
Network Eng: ticket opened with Azure Networking: INC-AZ-4567. Also capturing pcap and BGP RIB snapshots.
Sara P.: customer note sent to the 19 affected accounts (initial notification + expected actions). Will follow up with 1:1 for those requesting support.
incident-bot: Severity reduced to S3 at 2237000280 after region-wide error rates dropped below threshold for 10m. Monitoring continues.
Amanda C.: moving to monitoring/response. Oncall handoff: @Mike L. will take post-mortem lead, @Jonah R. will own telemetry artifacts, @Network Eng will track vendor RCA. Leave on-call until 2240000000 unless escalation.
Mike L.: ack. Will schedule postmortem and include action items: - Add cross-region resolver failover automation, - Add per-customer allowlist guidance, - Improve BGP session alerting, - Run weekly chaos test for DNS pathing.
CS Ops: I'll follow up with customers and provide timeline for permanent fixes.
incident-bot: Incident INC-202303 closed for active paging at 2237000365; status: mitigated (S3).
